text:
The candidate hypothesis proposes a highly specific experimental study evaluating electrostatic atomization with silicon dioxide nanoparticles in biolubricants during turning at 100 m/min, targeting precise quantitative thresholds (30% reduction in friction coefficient, 25% reduction in wear rate). 

In contrast, the provided evidence describes a comprehensive review paper summarizing the broader state of the art, physicochemical mechanisms, supply equipment, and machining performance (citing examples involving alumina nanoparticles, carbon nanotubes, and jatropha oil across turning, milling, and grinding). The evidence does not present or test the candidate hypothesis.

VERDICT: REJECT
